checkpoints.question: What is the primary function of a mantrap vestibule in preventing unauthorized facility access?

options.A: It physically admits only one person at a time, preventing tailgating regardless of social pressure
options.B: It uses biometric scanners to verify the identity of each person entering the facility
options.C: It delays an attacker long enough for security personnel to respond to an intrusion attempt
options.D: It logs the badge ID of every person who enters and detects duplicate card usage patterns

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines a mantrap vestibule as a double-door airlock that admits only one person at a time and physically prevents tailgating regardless of social pressure — the mechanism itself prevents sharing a single passage.

checkpoints.question: What type of fraud does a shimmer device enable that a traditional ATM skimmer overlay cannot?

options.A: Wireless data transmission using Bluetooth to send stolen data to a nearby accomplice
options.B: Magnetic stripe duplication that allows the attacker to use the card at point-of-sale terminals
options.C: Card-not-present fraud, enabling online purchases where no physical chip is needed
options.D: Real-time transaction monitoring that allows the attacker to intercept PIN codes during use

checkpoints.explanation: The section explicitly states that a shimmer device reads chip data and enables card-not-present fraud (online purchases where no physical chip is needed), whereas the traditional ATM skimmer overlay reads the magnetic stripe.

checkpoints.question: Why do contactless payment cards resist RFID cloning attacks while older HID proximity cards do not?

options.A: Contactless payment cards use longer-range RF signals that are harder to capture with cheap hardware
options.B: Contactless payment cards employ multi-factor authentication that requires a PIN at each point of sale
options.C: Contactless payment cards use stronger encryption algorithms that cannot be defeated with standard cloning tools
options.D: Contactless payment cards generate a dynamic cryptogram per transaction instead of broadcasting a static ID

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that contactless payment cards generate a dynamic cryptogram (one-time code) per transaction, so a static clone cannot complete a payment, while older cards lack this protection and broadcast a static ID that can be cloned.

checkpoints.question: How does a USB Rubber Ducky bypass both antivirus and application allowlisting defenses?

options.A: It disables antivirus signatures before they can scan incoming USB device firmware for malicious code
options.B: It emulates a USB keyboard and types pre-programmed commands, invoking legitimate OS utilities without writing files to disk
options.C: It copies approved system utilities into memory and executes them under their trusted certificate before allowlisting can block them
options.D: It exploits a vulnerability in the operating system's USB driver to gain administrative privileges before any security check

checkpoints.explanation: The section explains that USB Rubber Ducky and O.MG Cable bypass antivirus and allowlisting because they invoke legitimate OS utilities by typing commands — no file is written to disk, and they work by emulating a keyboard.

checkpoints.question: Which defense prevents data theft at a compromised public USB charging station while still allowing the device to charge?

options.A: A power-only USB cable that has data lines physically absent from the connector
options.B: A software firewall on the device that blocks all inbound connections during charging mode
options.C: An encryption module that encrypts all data transmitted over the USB charging connection in real time
options.D: A biometric lock on the charging port that requires fingerprint authentication before power is delivered

checkpoints.explanation: The section lists power-only USB cable as a defense for juice jacking — it has data lines physically absent, so power flows but no data can be stolen.

checkpoints.question: Why is full disk encryption alone insufficient to protect against a cold boot attack?

options.A: Full disk encryption is defeated by physically removing the storage device before the cold boot attack can execute
options.B: Full disk encryption protects stored data but not encryption keys already loaded into RAM that the attack can recover
options.C: Cold boot attacks bypass full disk encryption by using a firmware-level exploit to decrypt the storage automatically
options.D: Cold boot attacks access the encrypted disk through an out-of-band management interface that encrypts alone cannot defend

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that full disk encryption protects stored data but not keys already loaded into RAM, which is what a cold boot attack exploits by recovering data from DRAM after power-off.

checkpoints.question: What is the primary purpose of using tamper-evident chassis seals as a defense against hardware implants?

options.A: To encrypt all data traveling across internal buses and prevent unauthorized hardware from intercepting communications
options.B: To physically disable the device's motherboard if the seal is broken, destroying any implant that was inserted
options.C: To prevent the physical installation of backdoor devices inside equipment by making tampering visually obvious
options.D: To alert security personnel immediately when someone opens the chassis by triggering an electronic alarm

checkpoints.explanation: The section lists tamper-evident chassis seals as a defense against implant installation, enabling detection of hardware changes through visible evidence of tampering.

checkpoints.question: Which type of environmental attack causes facility-wide outages by targeting the infrastructure computing equipment depends on?

options.A: Activating fire suppression systems that displace oxygen and interfere with network connectivity
options.B: Flooding from overhead plumbing or external water intrusion that causes corrosion of data center hardware
options.C: Cutting external electrical panels or HVAC units to disable power and cooling systems simultaneously
options.D: Cutting external electrical panels or draining generator fuel to cause facility-wide power loss

checkpoints.explanation: The section identifies power attacks as cutting external electrical panels or draining generator fuel, which cause facility-wide outage by affecting the infrastructure that computing equipment depends on.
